''Štajerski ponos'' (The pride of [[Styria (Slovenia)|Styria]]) | founded = {{Start date and age|df=yes|1960|12|12}} | ground = [[Ljudski vrt]] | capacity = 11,709 | chrtitle = President | chairman = Uroš Mlakar | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Darko Milanič]] | league = [[Slovenian PrvaLiga]] | season = [[2025–26 Slovenian PrvaLiga|2025–26]] | position = Slovenian PrvaLiga, 5th of 10 | pattern_la1 =_maribor2627h | pattern_b1 = _maribor2627h | pattern_ra1 =_maribor2627h | pattern_sh1 = _maribor2627h | pattern_so1 = _maribor2627hl | leftarm1 = 373C7D | body1 = 373C7D | rightarm1 = 373C7D | shorts1 =373C7D | socks1 = 373C7D | pattern_la2 = _maribor2627a | pattern_b2 = _maribor2627a | pattern_ra2 = _maribor2627a | pattern_sh2 = _maribor2627a | pattern_so2 = _maribor2627al | leftarm2 = FFFFFF | body2 = FFFFFF | rightarm2 = FFFFFF | shorts2 = FFFFFF | socks2 = FFFFFF | pattern_la3 = _maribor2627t | pattern_b3 = _maribor2627t | pattern_ra3 = _maribor2627t | pattern_sh3 = _maribor2627t | pattern_so3 = _maribor2627tl | leftarm3 = | body3 = | rightarm3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = | current = | website = {{URL|https://www.nkmaribor.com/}} }} '''Nogometni klub Maribor''' ({{langx|en|Maribor Football Club}}) is a Slovenian professional [[Association football|football]] club based in [[Maribor]], Slovenia. It competes in the [[Slovenian PrvaLiga]], the top tier of the [[Football in Slovenia#League system|Slovenian football league system]]. Nicknamed "The Purples" (''{{lang|sl|Vijoličasti}}''), the club was founded on 12 December 1960. They are regarded as a symbol of [[Football in Slovenia|Slovenian football]], particularly in their home region of [[Styria (Slovenia)|Styria]] in northeastern Slovenia. Maribor have won a record 16 Slovenian PrvaLiga titles, 9 [[Slovenian Football Cup|Slovenian Cups]] and 4 [[Slovenian Supercup]]s. The club won seven consecutive league titles between 1997 and 2003, and five consecutive titles between 2011 and 2015. Prior to Slovenia's [[Breakup of Yugoslavia|independence]] in 1991, Maribor played in the [[Yugoslav football league system|Yugoslav football system]]. They won the Yugoslav [[Yugoslav Second League|second division]] in [[1966–67 Yugoslav Second League|1967]] and were therefore promoted to the top-level [[Yugoslav First League]], where they stayed until 1972. They are one of three Slovenian teams that participated in the Yugoslavia's highest division between the end of [[World War II]] in 1945 and the breakup of Yugoslavia in 1991. Maribor is the only Slovenian club that reached the group stages of the [[UEFA Champions League]]. In addition, the club is one of the two founding members of the Slovenian PrvaLiga (along with [[NK Celje|Celje]]) which have never been relegated from the league since the inaugural 1991–92 season. The club have a long-standing rivalry with [[NK Olimpija Ljubljana|Olimpija]] from the capital [[Ljubljana]], with whom they contest the [[Eternal derby (Slovenia)|Eternal derby]]. Other rivalries include those with [[NK Celje|Celje]], dubbed as the Styrian derby, and the Prekmurje–Styria derby, contested between Maribor and [[NŠ Mura|Mura]]. Maribor's home ground is the [[Ljudski vrt]] stadium, which has a capacity of 11,709 seats. The traditional colours of the club are purple, yellow and white."}}
